Found critical ADHD logic fragmentation and semantic search duplication violating separation of concerns. PostgreSQL collision between Serena and ConPort AGE is highest priority blocking risk.",
./scripts/deploy/migration/conport_export.json:24:      "implementation_details": "Analysis documented in docs/CROSS-COMPONENT-ANALYSIS.md. ./scripts/deploy/migration/conport_export.json:70:      "rationale": "Comprehensive Zen thinkdeep analysis validated all architecture synthesis claims about search/retrieval layer. ./scripts/deploy/migration/conport_export.json:89:      "implementation_details": "**Fragmentation Evidence:**\n- Serena v2: 10 hardcoded limits (max_results=10, complexity_threshold=0.7, focus_limit=5, context_depth=3)\n- ADHD Engine: 15 thresholds (monitoring intervals 60-300s, energy levels 0.2-0.9, cognitive load 0.2-0.8)\n- ConPort KG: 5 values (flow_threshold=900s, context_switches=5, cognitive_load_threshold=0.7)\n- dope-context: 2 limits (top_n_display=10, max_cache=40)\n\n**Inconsistencies Found:**\n- Cognitive load \"high\" varies: 0.6 (Serena) vs 0.7 (ConPort) vs 0.8 (ADHD Engine)\n- Progressive disclosure: 10 (general) vs 5 (focus mode) vs 40 (cached)\n\n**Solution: ADHDConfigService Architecture**\n1. Create dopemux-core/adhd module with unified ADHDThresholds schema (30+ fields)\n2. Build ADHDConfigClient with 5-minute caching (<1ms cache hits)\n3. Enhance ADHD Engine with GET /api/v1/config/thresholds endpoint\n4. Migrate services with feature flags for gradual rollout\n5. Fallback to safe defaults for fault tolerance\n\n**Implementation Phases (7 days):**\n- Week 1: Foundation (dopemux-core module, 2d) + API layer (ADHD Engine endpoint, 1d)\n- Week 2: Migration (Serena\u2192dope-context\u2192ConPort, 3d) + Validation (1d)\n\n**Benefits:**\n- Zero hardcoded thresholds (100% centralized)\n- Consistent values across all services\n- User-specific personalization enabled\n- 75% reduction in maintenance burden\n- Easy A/B testing (change once, affects all)\n\n**Risk Mitigations:**\n- Network latency: 5-min client caching\n- ADHD Engine failure: Fallback to safe defaults\n- Migration complexity: Feature flags for gradual rollout\n- Performance: Staggered cache expiry for even load\n\n**Files Analyzed:**\n- /Users/hue/code/dopemux-mvp/services/serena/v2/adhd_features.py\n- /Users/hue/code/dopemux-mvp/services/adhd_engine/engine.py\n- /Users/hue/code/dopemux-mvp/services/adhd_engine/config.py\n- /Users/hue/code/dopemux-mvp/services/conport_kg/adhd_query_adapter.py\n- /Users/hue/code/dopemux-mvp/services/dope-context/src/rerank/voyage_reranker.py\n\n**Enhanced vs Synthesis:**\nExtends original Task 2.3 (2 days) with client library pattern, fault tolerance, performance optimization, and realistic 7-day timeline. Adds user personalization capability not in synthesis.",
./scripts/deploy/migration/conport_export.json:102:      "rationale": "Systematic Zen thinkdeep analysis revealed significant MCP infrastructure duplication and separation violations across 6 active MCP servers (pal, zen, conport, serena, gptr-mcp, claude-context). Found 5 infrastructure duplication categories: (1) API clients - 4 servers use OpenAI, 2 use VoyageAI with no coordination; (2) Embeddings - 2 separate pipelines (ConPort 384-dim vs dope-context 1024-dim); (3) Vector DBs - 3 approaches (Qdrant, Milvus, FTS); (4) Databases - ConPort split-brain across 2 PostgreSQL; (5) Coordination gap - DopeconBridge unused. Identified 3 separation violations: overlapping search (ConPort + dope-context), ADHD fragmentation (23+ thresholds across 4 servers), no shared utilities. 3-tier consolidation strategy maintains MCP independence while eliminating duplication through shared core library (dopemux-core), infrastructure consolidation (1 PostgreSQL, 1 Milvus, centralized embeddings), and clarified DopeconBridge routing (cross-plane only). Aligns with Decisions #4 (storage), #5 (search), #6 (ADHD).",
./scripts/deploy/migration/conport_export.json:103:      "implementation_details": "**Evidence from docker-compose.unified.yml:**\n- 6 active MCP servers: pal (3003), zen (3003), conport (3004), serena (3006), claude-context (3007), gptr-mcp (3009)\n- 2 disabled: task-master-ai (3005), leantime-bridge (3015)\n- Infrastructure: 2 PostgreSQL (5432, 5455), 2 Redis (6379, 6380), 1 MySQL (3306), 3 Milvus components, DopeconBridge (3016)\n\n**5 Infrastructure Duplication Categories:**\n1. **API Client Duplication**: OpenAI key in 4 servers (zen, conport, gptr-mcp, claude-context); VoyageAI in 2 (conport, claude-context) - no connection pooling or rate limit coordination\n2. **Embedding Service Duplication**: ConPort embedding_service.py (384-dim all-MiniLM) vs dope-context VoyageEmbedder (1024-dim) - 3x API cost, quality gap\n3. **Vector DB Redundancy**: Milvus (claude-context only), Qdrant (in-memory data loss), ConPort FTS fallback - migration incomplete\n4. **Database Split-Brain**: ConPort uses postgres-primary:5432 AND postgres-age:5455 - consistency risk per Decision #4\n5. **Coordination Gap**: DopeconBridge exists but MCP servers don't use it - direct service-to-service communication\n\n**3 Separation Violations:**\n1. **Overlapping Search**: ConPort + dope-context both do semantic search with different embeddings (Decision #5 resolves by removing ConPort search)\n2. **ADHD Fragmentation**: 23+ hardcoded thresholds across ADHD Engine (15), Serena (10), ConPort (5), dope-context (2) - Decision #6 resolves with ADHDConfigService\n3. **No Shared Infrastructure**: Each MCP isolated, duplicated code for API clients, caching, error handling\n\n**3-Tier Consolidation Strategy:**\n\n**Tier 1: Shared Core Library (dopemux-core)** - NEW\n- Unified API client manager (OpenAI, VoyageAI, Gemini) with connection pooling\n- Shared embedding service wrapper (delegates to dope-context)\n- ADHDConfigClient (connects to ADHDConfigService from Decision #6)\n- Common error handling, logging, health check patterns\n- Benefits: -60% code duplication, consistent API usage, centralized rate limiting\n- Timeline: 3 days\n\n**Tier 2: Infrastructure Consolidation** - CRITICAL\n- Database: Test PostgreSQL AGE+asyncpg compatibility (Task 1.1.1), merge or add sync layer (5d)\n- Vector DB: Complete Qdrant\u2192Milvus migration for dope-context (5d) - from Decision #4\n- Embeddings: Remove ConPort embedding_service.py, use dope-context only (1d) - from Decision #5\n- Timeline: 7 days (parallel tasks)\n\n**Tier 3: MCP Separation Strategy** - MAINTAIN INDEPENDENCE\n- Keep 6 MCP servers separate with distinct responsibilities:\n  * pal: External docs API (no infrastructure overlap)\n  * zen: Multi-model orchestration (stateless)\n  * conport: Decision authority (uses shared core for embeddings)\n  * serena: LSP server (filesystem cache, no DB)\n  * gptr-mcp: Research-specific (Tavily dependency)\n  * claude-context: Search authority (owns Milvus)\n- Rationale: Each has distinct responsibility per Two-Plane Architecture, no capability overlap after Decision #5\n- Timeline: 5 days for MCP updates to use dopemux-core\n\n**DopeconBridge Routing Rules** - CLARIFIED\n- **Cross-Plane Communication**: PM Plane \u2194 Cognitive Plane MUST route through DopeconBridge (port 3016)\n- **Cognitive Plane Internal**: Direct MCP-to-MCP allowed (same plane)\n- **Status Updates**: Only through Leantime Bridge \u2192 DopeconBridge \u2192 Leantime\n- **Decision Logging**: Direct to mcp-conport (cognitive plane authority)\n- Bridge responsibility: Event routing between planes, not general message bus\n\n**Implementation Roadmap (17 days):**\n- **Phase 1: Foundation** (Week 1, 5d): Create dopemux-core package (3d) + PostgreSQL AGE test (2d)\n- **Phase 2: Infrastructure** (Week 2, 7d): Qdrant\u2192Milvus (5d) + Remove ConPort embeddings (1d) + ADHD centralization (7d overlap)\n- **Phase 3: Integration** (Week 3, 5d): Update MCPs to use dopemux-core (3d) + Bridge routing rules (2d)\n\n**Expected Outcomes:**\n- Containers: 19 \u2192 16 (-16%)\n- Databases: 2 PostgreSQL \u2192 1 (or sync layer if AGE incompatible)\n- Vector DBs: 1 Milvus (remove Qdrant)\n- Code duplication: -60% through shared core\n- ADHD consistency: 100% via ADHDConfigService\n- Deployment complexity: -40%\n\n**Risk Mitigations:**\n- PostgreSQL AGE incompatibility \u2192 fallback sync layer\n- Migration complexity \u2192 feature flags for gradual rollout\n- Breaking changes \u2192 dopemux-core versioning with compatibility matrix\n\n**Files Analyzed:**\n- /Users/hue/code/dopemux-mvp/docker-compose.unified.yml\n- /Users/hue/code/dopemux-mvp/docs/ARCHITECTURE-CONSOLIDATION-SYNTHESIS.md\n- /Users/hue/code/dopemux-mvp/services/conport/src/context_portal_mcp/core/embedding_service.py\n- /Users/hue/code/dopemux-mvp/services/dope-context/src/search/hybrid_search.py\n\n**Validation:**\nAll findings cross-referenced with Decisions #4 (storage), #5 (search/retrieval), #6 (ADHD mechanisms) and architecture synthesis document. Strategy addresses root causes systematically with realistic timeline.",
./scripts/deploy/migration/conport_export.json:124:      "implementation_details": "**Evidence from docker-compose.unified.yml + DopeconBridge code:**\n\n**Service Communication Matrix**:\n- 6 active MCP servers: pal (3003), zen (3003), conport (3004), serena (3006), claude-context (3007), gptr-mcp (3009)\n- DopeconBridge (3016): Only 5 GET /kg/* endpoints (recent, summary, neighborhood, context, search)\n- NO MCP-to-MCP communication found (each MCP isolated)\n- Database: ConPort \u2192 postgres-primary:5432 AND postgres-age:5455 (split-brain)\n- Redis: Deployed as \"Event Bus & General Cache\" but unused for events\n\n**7 Anti-Patterns Identified:**\n\n**1. Phantom Orchestrator** (CRITICAL):\n- Documentation: \"DopeconBridge for cross-plane event routing and orchestration\"\n- Reality: Read-only KG gateway with 5 GET endpoints only\n- Missing: Write endpoints (POST/PUT), event routing, orchestration logic\n- Impact: False architectural assumptions, no actual cross-plane integration\n\n**2. Isolated Islands** (HIGH):\n- Zero MCP-to-MCP communication despite same Cognitive Plane\n- Each MCP completely isolated, no service coordination\n- Impact: No delegation, duplicated external API calls, no shared caching\n- Example: mcp-claude-context and mcp-conport both call VoyageAI independently\n\n**3. Unknown Decision Flow** (CRITICAL):\n- Cannot trace how decisions get logged in ConPort\n- DopeconBridge is read-only (no POST/PUT)\n- No MCP-to-MCP calls found\n- Impact: Core functionality undocumented, can't validate decisions actually logged\n\n**4. Redis Ghost Bus** (MEDIUM):\n- Redis deployed as \"Event Bus & General Cache\" (docker-compose line 13)\n- No pub/sub usage found, no event-driven communication\n- Only ADHD Engine uses Redis for state storage\n- Impact: Wasted infrastructure, event bus capability unused\n\n**5. Synchronous API Gauntlet** (MEDIUM):\n- 4 MCPs independently call OpenAI (zen, conport, gptr-mcp, claude-context)\n- 2 MCPs independently call VoyageAI (conport, claude-context)\n- No connection pooling, no rate limit coordination\n- Impact: 3-4x API costs, potential rate limit violations, no deduplication\n\n**6. ConPort Split-Brain Communication** (CRITICAL - from Decision #4):\n- ConPort writes to TWO PostgreSQL: primary:5432 + age:5455\n- DopeconBridge queries postgres-age (third dependency)\n- Impact: Data consistency risk, transaction boundaries unclear\n\n**7. No Circuit Breakers** (LOW):\n- No fault isolation between services\n- If OpenAI fails, 4 MCP servers fail simultaneously\n- No graceful degradation or retry coordination\n\n**Communication Patterns Analysis:**\n\n**Actual Patterns** (Evidence-based):\n1. Client \u2192 MCP: stdio/SSE on ports 3003-3009 (working)\n2. MCP \u2192 Infrastructure: Direct DB/API calls (working but duplicated)\n3. PM \u2192 Cognitive (read): Leantime \u2192 DopeconBridge \u2192 ConPort KG (working, limited)\n4. Cognitive Internal: NONE (expected but not implemented)\n\n**Missing Patterns** (Documented but absent):\n1. Cross-plane write operations\n2. Event routing (pub/sub)\n3. MCP orchestration/coordination\n4. Shared infrastructure (connection pooling)\n\n**7-Part Optimization Strategy:**\n\n**Optimization #1: Complete DopeconBridge** (9 days, CRITICAL):\n- Add write endpoints: POST /kg/decisions, PUT /kg/decisions/{id}, POST /events/publish\n- Event routing layer: Redis pub/sub for async events (DecisionCreated, TaskStatusChanged, ADHDStateUpdated)\n- Authority enforcement: Validate x_source_plane, PM (read+events), Cognitive (full CRUD)\n- Timeline: 9 days (parallel with dopemux-core)\n\n**Optimization #2: MCP Service Mesh** (7 days, HIGH):\n- Service registry in Redis (service_name \u2192 host:port, health checks every 30s)\n- MCP internal API: JSON-RPC over HTTP for mcp-A \u2192 mcp-B\n- Request deduplication: Hash-based with 5s window, cache in Redis\n- Timeline: 7 days (Week 2)\n\n**Optimization #3: Shared API Client Pool** (3 days, HIGH - from Decision #7):\n- dopemux-core package with unified OpenAI/VoyageAI/Gemini clients\n- Connection pooling (max 10 concurrent), rate limit coordination\n- Benefits: -75% API calls through deduplication\n- Timeline: 3 days (Phase 1 of Decision #7)\n\n**Optimization #4: Fix Unknown Decision Flow** (4 days, CRITICAL):\n- Document current flow: Trace ConPort MCP database writes\n- Implement standard flow: Any service \u2192 mcp-conport.log_decision() \u2192 postgres-age\n- Tracing: Add request_id header for end-to-end tracking\n- Timeline: 4 days (Week 2)\n\n**Optimization #5: Activate Redis Event Bus** (4 days, MEDIUM):\n- Event channels: pm_plane_events, cognitive_plane_events, adhd_events, cross_plane_events\n- Publisher/Subscriber: DopeconBridge (cross-plane), ADHD Engine (state), Leantime Bridge (tasks)\n- Event schema with event_type, source_plane, source_service, payload, timestamp\n- Timeline: 4 days (Week 2)\n\n**Optimization #6: Resolve ConPort Split-Brain** (from Decision #4):\n- Test PostgreSQL AGE+asyncpg compatibility (Task 1.1.1 already scheduled)\n- Merge to postgres-primary if compatible, or add sync layer\n- Update DopeconBridge to single source of truth\n\n**Optimization #7: Circuit Breakers** (included in dopemux-core):\n- Tenacity library with exponential backoff\n- Part of 3-day dopemux-core development\n\n**Integrated Optimization Roadmap:**\n\n**Phase 1: Foundation** (Week 1, 9 days - parallel):\n- Task 1.1: Create dopemux-core with API clients (3d) [Decision #7]\n- Task 1.2: Test PostgreSQL AGE compatibility (2d) [Decision #4]\n- Task 1.3: Complete DopeconBridge (9d - parallel):\n  * Subtask A: Add write endpoints (3d)\n  * Subtask B: Event routing layer (4d)\n  * Subtask C: Authority enforcement (2d)\n\n**Phase 2: Service Mesh & Flows** (Week 2, 7 days):\n- Task 2.1: Implement MCP service mesh (7d)\n- Task 2.2: Document & fix decision flow (4d)\n- Task 2.3: Activate Redis event bus (4d)\n- Task 2.4: Remove ConPort embeddings (1d) [Decision #5]\n- Task 2.5: Migrate Qdrant\u2192Milvus (5d) [Decision #4]\n\n**Phase 3: Integration & Validation** (Week 3, 5 days):\n- Task 3.1: Update all MCPs to use dopemux-core (3d) [Decision #7]\n- Task 3.2: Implement cross-plane event flows (2d)\n- Task 3.3: End-to-end integration testing (3d)\n\n**Timeline Update**: Extends Decision #7 from 17 to 21 days (+4 days for data flow)\n\n**Expected Outcomes:**\n\n**Performance**:\n- -75% external API calls (deduplication + pooling)\n- -60% latency for cross-plane queries (direct mesh vs gateway)\n- +200% throughput (async event-driven vs sync)\n\n**Reliability**:\n- Circuit breakers prevent cascade failures\n- Event-driven reduces coupling\n- Service mesh enables graceful degradation\n\n**Clarity**:\n- Documented decision flow (traceable end-to-end)\n- DopeconBridge implements actual design\n- MCP communication patterns explicit\n\n**Cost**:\n- -$300/month API costs (fewer duplicate calls)\n- Same infrastructure (utilize existing Redis)\n\n**Risk Mitigations**:\n- DopeconBridge changes: Feature ./scripts/deploy/migration/conport_export.json:541:      "rationale": "**PROBLEM**: Significant infrastructure duplication across 3 categories creates operational overhead, memory waste, and maintenance complexity.\n\n**EVIDENCE**:\n**PostgreSQL (3 instances \u2192 should be 1)**:\n- `dopemux-postgres` (5432) \u2192 dopemux_memory \u2192 **ORPHANED** (conport-memory service disabled)\n- `dopemux-postgres-age` (5455) \u2192 dopemux_knowledge_graph (AGE) \u2192 **ACTIVE** (ConPort MCP)\n- `conport-kg-postgres-age` (5455) \u2192 **DEFERRED + PORT CONFLICT**\n\n**Redis (4+ instances \u2192 should be 2-3)**:\n- `dopemux-redis-primary` \u2192 ConPort MCP caching \u2192 **ACTIVE but unnamed in compose**\n- `dopemux-redis-events` (6379) \u2192 Event bus \u2192 **ACTIVE**\n- `conport-kg-redis` (6379) \u2192 **DEFERRED**\n- `redis_leantime` \u2192 PM plane (Leantime) \u2192 **APPROPRIATE ISOLATION**\n\n**Vector Databases (2 types \u2192 should be 1)**:\n- **Milvus** (3-service stack: milvus+etcd+minio) \u2192 claude-context MCP \u2192 **HIGH COMPLEXITY**\n- **Qdrant** (1-service) \u2192 dope-context MCP \u2192 **SIMPLE, MODERN**\n\n**TWO-PLANE ANALYSIS**:\n- **Cognitive Plane**: ConPort (PostgreSQL AGE + Redis), Serena, dope-context (Qdrant)\n- **PM Plane**: Leantime (isolated Redis + MySQL) \u2705 Correct separation\n- **Shared Infrastructure**: Event bus (Redis) bridges both planes \u2705 Appropriate\n\n**ROOT CAUSE**: Incomplete migration from old memory-stack architecture to new MCP-integrated ConPort. DEFERRED conport-kg deployment was never activated.",
./scripts/deploy/migration/conport_export.json:542:      "implementation_details": "**CONSOLIDATION STRATEGY (3-Phase)**:\n\n**PHASE 1: PostgreSQL Consolidation** (Immediate - Low Risk)\n- **Action**: Decommission `dopemux-postgres` (orphaned) and `conport-kg-postgres-age` (DEFERRED)\n- **Target**: Single `dopemux-postgres-age` (5455) as authoritative knowledge graph DB\n- **Migration**: None required (memory-stack/conport-memory already disabled)\n- **Savings**: 2 PostgreSQL containers eliminated\n- **Risk**: NONE (removing unused infrastructure)\n\n**PHASE 2: Redis Consolidation** (Medium Priority - Medium Risk)\n- **Target Architecture**:\n  1. `dopemux-redis-shared` (6379) \u2192 ConPort caching + general MCP cache\n  2. `dopemux-redis-events` (6380) \u2192 Event bus (separate for isolation)\n  3. `redis_leantime` \u2192 PM plane (keep isolated per two-plane architecture)\n- **Action**: \n  - Deploy `dopemux-redis-shared` in mcp-network\n  - Update ConPort MCP to use dopemux-redis-shared instead of dopemux-redis-primary\n  - Remove conport-kg-redis (DEFERRED)\n- **Savings**: Consolidate primary + conport-kg into shared instance\n- **Risk**: MEDIUM (requires ConPort config update, but Redis data is cache = non-critical)\n\n**PHASE 3: Vector DB Migration** (Lower Priority - Medium-High Risk)\n- **Action**: Migrate claude-context from Milvus \u2192 Qdrant\n- **Rationale**: \n  - Milvus = 3 services (milvus+etcd+minio) = high operational overhead\n  - Qdrant = 1 service = simpler, modern, already proven with dope-context\n  - dope-context (Qdrant) demonstrates this works well\n- **Migration Path**:\n  1. Deploy claude-context-qdrant collection in existing mcp-qdrant\n  2. Re-index workspaces into Qdrant\n  3. Update claude-context MCP to use Qdrant\n  4. Decommission Milvus stack (3 containers eliminated)\n- **Savings**: 3 containers (milvus, etcd, minio) + simplified operations\n- **Risk**: MEDIUM-HIGH (data migration, re-indexing time, potential embedding compatibility issues)\n\n**OPERATIONAL SAVINGS**:\n- **Containers**: 8 eliminated (2 PostgreSQL + 3 Milvus stack + 1 Redis + 1 DEFERRED Redis + 1 DEFERRED PostgreSQL)\n- **Memory**: ~2-3GB saved (PostgreSQL ~500MB each, Milvus stack ~1.5GB, Redis ~200MB each)\n- **Maintenance**: Single PostgreSQL AGE, 2-3 Redis, 1 Qdrant vs current sprawl\n- **Port Conflicts**: Resolved (5455 conflict eliminated)\n\n**AUTHORITY COMPLIANCE**:\n- \u2705 PM/Cognitive separation maintained (Leantime Redis isolated)\n- \u2705 ConPort remains sole knowledge graph authority (PostgreSQL AGE)\n- \u2705 Event bus remains shared coordination layer (Redis events)\n- \u2705 No cross-plane data sharing violations",

./scripts/deploy/migration/conport_export.json:606:      "rationale": "**PROBLEM**: Current approach runs 3 separate dopemux instances (one per worktree), leading to:\n- Fragmented ConPort knowledge (each instance has own database connection)\n- Duplicate MCP server processes (Serena, ConPort stdio per instance)\n- No unified orchestration or cross-worktree awareness\n- 9 CLI processes with no coordination\n\n**USER REQUIREMENT**: \"1 dopemux spawning multiple CLI tools is the right approach. Unified knowledge but tagged per instance.\"\n\n**DISCOVERY**: Zen MCP's clink tool supports `working_dir` parameter (clink/models.py:48, clink/agents/base.py:116), enabling worktree-specific CLI spawning from single orchestrator.\n\n**ARCHITECTURE INSIGHT**:\nCurrent state (What's running NOW):\n- 3x `dopemux start` processes (main, worktree-test, ui-build)\n- Each spawns: Claude Code + Serena + ConPort\n- No communication between instances\n\nProposed state (Zen clink-enabled):\n- 1x dopemux orchestrator (main worktree)\n- Spawns CLI instances via clink with different working_dir\n- Unified ConPort knowledge graph with session_id tagging\n- Shared MCP services (Serena, dope-context, etc.)\n\n**KEY CAPABILITY UNLOCKED**:\n```json\n// conf/cli_clients/claude-ui.json\n{\n  \"working_dir\": \"/Users/hue/code/ui-build\",  // \u2190 Runs in ui-build worktree!\n  ...\n}\n```\n\nThen from main dopemux instance:\n```\nclink with claude-ui to build dashboard component  // Runs in ui-build worktree\nclink with claude-test to add integration tests     // Runs in test worktree\nclink with claude-main to implement auth           // Runs in main worktree\n```\n\n**COMPARISON TO OLD MULTI-INSTANCE DOCKER** (Decision #29 - removed):\n- OLD: MetaMCP broker with PORT_BASE offsets (3000, 3030, 3060)\n- OLD: Instance-specific container naming (CONTAINER_PREFIX)\n- OLD: Complex environment variable management\n- NEW: Simple working_dir in CLI config\n- NEW: Zen's clink handles orchestration\n- NEW: Native git worktree isolation (no Docker complexity)",

/Users/hue/code/dopemux-worktree-test\n\n**ARCHITECTURE DESIGN**:\n\n**Tier 1: Dopemux Orchestrator** (Single Instance)\n- Runs in main worktree: /Users/hue/code/dopemux-mvp\n- Provides: CLI coordination, ConPort access, shared MCP services\n- Entry point: `dopemux start` (no multi-instance detection needed)\n\n**Tier 2: Shared MCP Services** (Single Set)\n- ConPort MCP (stdio): Unified engine with clink\n- PAL apilookup, GPT-Researcher, etc.: Shared by all CLI instances\n\n**Tier 3: Spawned CLI Instances** (Via Zen Clink)\n- `clink with claude-main` \u2192 Works in /dopemux-mvp\n- `clink with claude-ui` \u2192 Works in /ui-build\n- `clink with claude-test` \u2192 Works in /worktree-test\n- `clink with codex` \u2192 Can target any worktree\n- `clink with gemini` \u2192 Can target any worktree\n\n**ConPort Knowledge Graph Strategy**:\n\n**Unified Graph with Session Tagging**:\n```python\n# Each clink spawn gets unique session_id\nsession_id = f\"{cli_name}-{worktree_name}-{timestamp}\"\n\n# Active context tracks per-session\nactive_context = {\n  \"workspace_id\": \"/Users/hue/code/dopemux-mvp\",  # Always main repo\n  \"session_id\": \"claude-ui-20251016-0740\",\n  \"worktree_path\": \"/Users/hue/code/ui-build\",\n  \"branch\": \"ui-build\",\n  \"current_focus\": \"Dashboard component\"\n}\n\n# Shared knowledge (all sessions see):\n- Decisions (architectural choices apply to all worktrees)\n- System patterns (coding standards unified)\n- Cross-worktree progress (see what's happening everywhere)\n\n# Session-specific (isolated per CLI spawn):\n- current_focus (each CLI has own task)\n- session_start, session_duration\n- attention_state, energy_level\n```\n\n**IMPLEMENTATION PHASES**:\n\n**Phase 1: Enable Clink Worktree Support** (1-2 days)\n- \u2705 Create worktree-specific CLI configs (DONE)\n- \u2610 Restart Zen MCP to load configs\n- \u2610 Test basic clink spawning with working_dir\n- \u2610 Validate each CLI runs in correct worktree\n- \u2610 Confirm file operations respect working_dir\n\n**Phase 2: ConPort Session Management** (2-3 days)\n- \u2610 Update active_context schema: Add session_id, worktree_path, branch\n- \u2610 Modify ConPort MCP to accept session_id parameter\n- \u2610 Implement session tagging for all ConPort operations\n- \u2610 Add query filters: get_active_context(session_id=X)\n- \u2610 Dashboard shows all active sessions\n\n**Phase 3: Dopemux Orchestrator CLI** (3-4 days)\n- \u2610 `dopemux spawn claude-ui` \u2192 Wrapper for `clink with claude-ui`\n- \u2610 `dopemux spawn codex-main planner` \u2192 With role selection\n- \u2610 `dopemux sessions list` \u2192 Show all active clink sessions\n- \u2610 `dopemux sessions switch <id>` \u2192 Interactive session management\n- \u2610 Integration with dopemux UI (terminal dashboard)\n\n**Phase 4: Chat-Driven Development** (Future)\n- \u2610 `dopemux chat` \u2192 Zen chat tool as orchestrator\n- \u2610 Natural language: \"work on auth in main, ui in ui-build simultaneously\"\n- \u2610 Chat spawns appropriate clink instances automatically\n- \u2610 Coordinates multiple CLI agents for complex multi-worktree work\n\n**MIGRATION PATH** (From Current 3-Dopemux Setup):\n\n**Current State**:\n```bash\nTerminal 1: dopemux start  # in /dopemux-mvp\nTerminal 2: dopemux start  # in /ui-build  \nTerminal 3: dopemux start  # in /worktree-test\n```\n\n**Transition State** (Both work during migration):\n```bash\nTerminal 1: dopemux start  # Main orchestrator\n  > clink with claude-ui to build dashboard\n  > clink with claude-test to add tests\n\nTerminal 2/3: dopemux start  # Still available for heavy focused work\n```\n\n**Target State**:\n```bash\nSingle Terminal: dopemux start  # Orchestrates everything\n  > dopemux spawn claude-ui --task \"build dashboard\"\n  > dopemux spawn claude-test --task \"add integration tests\"  \n  > dopemux spawn codex-main planner --task \"plan auth migration\"\n  > dopemux sessions list  # See all active work\n```\n\n**ADHD BENEFITS**:\n- **Context Preservation**: Unified ConPort = no lost decisions across worktrees\n- **Reduced Cognitive Load**: Single entry point vs tracking 3 terminals\n- **Progressive Disclosure**: `dopemux sessions list` shows all work at glance\n- **Flexible Focus**: Spawn work in any worktree without leaving main session\n- **Parallel Work**: Multiple CLI instances run simultaneously, report back to orchestrator\n\n**TECHNICAL ADVANTAGES**:\n- Shared MCP services (1 Serena vs 3, 1 ConPort connection vs 3)\n- Unified knowledge graph (decisions visible across all work)\n- Better resource efficiency (fewer duplicate processes)\n- Simpler mental model (1 orchestrator vs N instances)\n\n**OPEN QUESTIONS** (Need Research/Testing):\n1. Can clink pass MCP server connections to spawned CLIs?\n2. How do spawned CLIs authenticate (inherit parent OAuth or separate)?\n3. Performance: Can 1 dopemux handle 3-5 concurrent clink spawns?\n4. Resource limits: Memory/CPU with multiple CLIs?\n5. Crash isolation: Does 1 failed clink spawn kill orchestrator?",

./scripts/deploy/migration/conport_export.json:640:      "implementation_details": "**Enhancements Implemented:**\n1. **OpenAI Context Generator** (src/context/openai_generator.py): gpt-5-mini for code descriptions, $0.05 per 50 files\n2. **Tree-sitter v0.25.2 Upgrade**: Enables Language(capsule) pattern, AST-aware chunking now operational\n3. **UUID Point IDs**: Convert SHA256 hashes to proper UUIDs for Qdrant compatibility\n4. **Docs Token Validation**: 8K limit with word-by-word splitting for >32K token docs\n5. **Unified SearchResult**: Support both code (`raw_code`, `file_path`) and docs (`text`, `source_path`) payloads\n\n**Validation Results:**\n- Code: 158 chunks from 50 files with complexity scores (0.16-0.32)\n- Docs: 428 chunks from markdown documentation\n- Search: <2s response, 0.43-0.73 relevance scores\n- ADHD: Progressive disclosure (max 10), complexity scoring, context snippets all working\n- Cost: $0.052 for 50 code files with context generation\n\n**Test Coverage:**\n- AST chunking validated with 6 semantic chunks (functions, classes, methods)\n- Search profiles tested: implementation, debugging, exploration\n- Unified search: Code + docs parallel retrieval working\n- Workspace isolation: MD5-based collection naming verified\n\nSee services/dope-context/FINAL_TEST_REPORT.md for complete validation report.",

./scripts/deploy/migration/conport_export.json:657:      "rationale": "Conducted ultra-thorough validation of git worktree support across all Dopemux MCP servers. ./scripts/deploy/migration/conport_export.json:658:      "implementation_details": "**Validation Results:**\n\n**3 Worktrees Tested:**\n- Main: /Users/hue/code/dopemux-mvp (hash: 3ca12e07)\n- ui-build: /Users/hue/code/ui-build (hash: 74c73f14)\n- worktree-test: /Users/hue/code/dopemux-worktree-test (hash: 37084b2c)\n\n**MCP Server Support:**\n1. **Dope-Context** (Native Python detection):\n   - Method: Walk up from cwd looking for .git (file or directory)\n   - Collections: code_{hash}, docs_{hash} per worktree\n   - Snapshots: ~/.dope-context/snapshots/{hash}/ per worktree\n   - Status: \u2705 Perfect isolation, automatic detection\n\n2. **ConPort** (Wrapper-based detection):\n   - Method: git rev-parse --show-toplevel in wrapper script\n   - Context: Separate context_portal directory per worktree\n   - Database: PostgreSQL rows keyed by workspace_id (absolute path)\n   - Status: \u2705 Full worktree awareness, strong indicators detected\n\n3. **Serena** (Wrapper-based detection):\n   - Method: git rev-parse --show-toplevel in wrapper script\n   - Docker: WORKSPACE_PATH env variable passed to container\n   - LSP: Operates within detected workspace\n   - Status: \u2705 Worktree-scoped operations\n\n**Isolation Verified:**\n- \u2705 Unique hashes: 3 worktrees = 3 distinct MD5 hashes\n- \u2705 Separate Qdrant collections (6 total: 3 code + 3 docs)\n- \u2705 Separate ConPort contexts (3 context_portal databases)\n- \u2705 No cross-worktree data leakage\n- \u2705 Search results properly scoped\n\n**ADHD Benefits:**\n- Physical directory = mental workspace boundary\n- Search results always relevant to current work\n- No confusion between main and feature branch code\n- Context switches are explicit (cd to different directory)\n- Parallel work supported without interference\n\n**Identified Gaps (Non-Blocking):**\n1. ./scripts/deploy/migration/conport_export.json:1121:      "rationale": "Implemented critical fixes to make dope-context production-ready and align with Anthropic's contextual retrieval research. Key improvements: (1) Comprehensive error handling with helpful messages for collection not found, API failures, and network issues, (2) BM25 index building and persistence after indexing - closes 14% retrieval quality gap from Anthropic research, (3) LRU component caching for VoyageEmbedder, VoyageReranker, MultiVectorSearch, DocumentSearch - reduces per-search overhead from ~500ms to ~50ms, (4) True incremental indexing with auto_reindex parameter - only updates changed files and rebuilds BM25. Now matches Anthropic's full contextual retrieval pipeline: contextual embeddings (35%) + BM25 (14%) + reranking (18%) = 67% error reduction.",

./scripts/deploy/migration/conport_export.json:2081:      "summary": "Fix MCP token limit errors in dope-context with progressive truncation",
./scripts/deploy/migration/conport_export.json:2082:      "rationale": "MCP responses exceeding 10K tokens cause hard failures in Claude Code's transport layer. Dope-context search_code was returning full code snippets (5K+ chars each) \u00d7 10 results = 12K+ tokens, exceeding limit. Root cause: no token budget management in MCP response construction.\n\nSolution: Implemented 3-layer token budget system:\n1. Per-item truncation (2K chars/code snippet \u2248 500 tokens)\n2. Total budget tracking (9K target with 10% headroom)\n3. Progressive truncation (highest-scored results preserved, lower scores dropped if budget exceeded)\n\nValidation: All tests pass. Realistic 10-result search uses 39% of budget (3.5K/9K tokens), well under 10K MCP limit.",
./scripts/deploy/migration/conport_export.json:2083:      "implementation_details": "Files created:\n- services/dope-context/src/utils/token_budget.py (330 lines)\n  - estimate_tokens(): 1 token \u2248 4 chars (conservative)\n  - truncate_code_results(): Per-item + total budget enforcement\n  - truncate_docs_results(): Same for docs\n  - TruncationResult dataclass: Transparency about what was truncated\n\nFiles modified:\n- services/dope-context/src/mcp/server.py (4 changes)\n  - Added import: from ..utils.token_budget import truncate_code_results, truncate_docs_results\n  - Updated _search_code_impl(): Added budget_tokens parameter (default 9000)\n  - Updated _docs_search_impl(): Added budget_tokens parameter (default 9000)\n  - Modified search_all(): Split budget (4K code + 4K docs = 8K total)\n\nBudget allocation:\n- search_code standalone: 9K tokens (10% headroom)\n- docs_search standalone: 9K tokens\n- search_all combined: 4K + 4K + 1K overhead = 9K total\n\nADHD benefits:\n- Progressive disclosure preserved (highest-scored results intact)\n- Transparency (truncated field shows what was cut)\n- Consistent behavior (no random failures)\n\nTesting: test_token_limit_fix.py validates all scenarios pass with <10K tokens",
./scripts/deploy/migration/conport_export.json:2087:        "dope-context",
./scripts/deploy/migration/conport_export.json:2096:      "rationale": "After fixing dope-context token limit issue (Decision #137), conducted comprehensive audit of all Dopemux MCP servers for similar vulnerabilities. Discovery: 10K token limit is a cross-cutting concern affecting ALL servers returning variable-sized content.\n\n**Audit Results**:\n- \ud83d\udd34 P0 Critical: Serena-v2 (read_file on large files), Desktop-Commander (base64 screenshots = 168K tokens!)\n- \ud83d\udfe1 P1 Medium: ConPort (bulk queries 100+ items), Zen (multi-step analysis accumulation)\n- \ud83d\udfe1 P2 Low: GPT-Researcher (research reports with many sources)\n- \u2705 Fixed: Dope-Context (3-layer progressive truncation)\n- \ud83d\udfe2 External: PAL apilookup (not our code)\n\n**Critical Insights**:\n1. Base64 encoding kills budgets: 2MB screenshot \u2192 168K tokens (17\u00d7 over limit!)\n2. File reading without limits: package-lock.json (200KB) = 50K tokens\n3. Bulk queries need progressive truncation: 100 decisions \u00d7 150 tokens = 15K tokens\n4. Multi-step tools accumulate context: 10-step analysis = 20K tokens\n\n**Recommended Pattern**: Create shared `mcp_response_budget` utility for all servers to use.",
./scripts/deploy/migration/conport_export.json:2110:      "rationale": "Following successful dope-context fix (Decision #137) and system-wide audit (Decision #138), Serena-v2 read_file identified as P0 critical vulnerability. Large files (package-lock.json = 200KB) could generate 112K tokens, causing hard MCP failures with no recovery. Fix implements 2-layer defense: max_lines=500 (ADHD-safe chunks) + max_tokens=9000 (MCP safety margin).",
./scripts/deploy/migration/conport_export.json:2139:      "rationale": "Audit (Decision #138) identified ConPort bulk queries as P1 vulnerability (15K+ tokens possible). Zen ultrathink analysis (gpt-5-pro) revealed simple limit enforcement insufficient: 50 decisions with full fields = 20K+ tokens. Progressive truncation only viable solution: build response item-by-item, track tokens, stop at 9K budget. Matches proven pattern from dope-context (Decision #137) and Serena (Decision #139).",
./scripts/deploy/migration/conport_export.json:2169:      "rationale": "User investigation revealed 4 critical bugs breaking ADHD context preservation:\n\n1. **CWD vs Git Root**: CLI used Path.cwd() instead of git root detection, breaking workspace detection from subdirectories and completely failing for worktrees.\n\n2. **Environment Not Passed**: MCP server startup subprocess didn't receive instance environment variables, making DOPEMUX_WORKSPACE_ID invisible to docker-compose. ALL instances used hardcoded default workspace.\n\n3. **Wrong Workspace in Env**: instance_manager.py set DOPEMUX_WORKSPACE_ID to main repo root instead of current worktree (actual_workspace). Instance B logged decisions to Instance A's workspace.\n\n4. **Fixed Ports**: docker-compose.yml used hardcoded ports (3004, 3006) preventing multi-instance from working at all - second instance failed with port conflicts.\n\n**Impact**: Context restoration broken, decisions logged to wrong projects, multi-instance completely non-functional. Core ADHD optimization promise (context preservation across interruptions) was broken.\n\n**Investigation Method**: Used dope-context search_code to find startup flow, grep to trace environment variable propagation, analyzed docker-compose for port configuration. Systematic code review revealed the issues were interconnected - fixing one without others wouldn't work.",
./scripts/deploy/migration/conport_export.json:2239:      "rationale": "User frustrated with manual worktree configuration and silent failures. Gap is 78% - critical misalignment with core value proposition.",
./scripts/deploy/migration/conport_export.json:2240:      "implementation_details": "**Recommended 3-Phase Solution** (~10 hours total):\n\n**PHASE 1: Fix Critical Bugs** (2 hours, HIGH PRIORITY)\n- Extract shared workspace detection to dopemux-core/workspace.py\n- Fix dope-context .git directory \u2192 file check for worktree compatibility  \n- Export DOPEMUX_WORKSPACE_ROOT from all MCP wrappers (fail-safe)\n- Update serena to use shared detection\n**Impact**: Eliminates 3 bugs, ensures consistency, low risk\n\n**PHASE 2: Auto-Configuration** (4 hours, MEDIUM PRIORITY)  \n- Create auto_configurator.py with dynamic path generation\n- Hook into dopemux start (auto-config current workspace)\n- Hook into dwt command (auto-config target worktree)\n- Remove manual configure-worktree-mcp.sh script\n**Impact**: Manual steps 5 \u2192 0, multi-user portable, low risk\n\n**PHASE 3: Seamless UX** (4 hours, NICE-TO-HAVE)\n- Auto-install shell integration on first dopemux start (opt-in)\n- Worktree template system (copy main \u2192 new worktree config)\n- Add dopemux doctor --worktree (diagnostics)\n- Comprehensive error messages + troubleshooting\n**Impact**: ADHD cognitive load 9/10 \u2192 2/10 (78% reduction), medium risk\n\n**Success Metrics**:\n- Manual steps: 5 \u2192 0 (100% reduction)\n- Cognitive load: 9/10 \u2192 2/10 (78% improvement)\n- Implementations: 3 \u2192 1 (consistency \u2705)\n- Silent failures: High \u2192 None (reliability \u2705)\n- Portability: Single-user \u2192 Multi-user (scalability \u2705)\n\n**Files to Modify**:\n- NEW: dopemux-core/workspace.py (shared detection)\n- MODIFY: services/dope-context/src/utils/workspace.py (use shared)\n- MODIFY: services/serena/v2/enhanced_lsp.py (use shared)\n- MODIFY: scripts/mcp-wrappers/*.sh (export env var)\n- NEW: src/dopemux/auto_configurator.py (auto-config system)\n- MODIFY: src/dopemux/cli.py (hooks for auto-config)\n- DELETE: scripts/configure-worktree-mcp.sh (replaced by auto-config)",

./scripts/deploy/migration/conport_export.json:3247:      "rationale": "Investigation revealed dope-context has excellent foundation (robust sync via SHA256 Merkle DAG, proven indexing pipeline, 98.9% test coverage, ADHD features) but requires manual user intervention for every sync cycle. Never use bash cat/grep/find or native Read/Grep tools for code.\n\nCORRECT USAGE:\n- Read files: mcp__serena-v2__read_file(relative_path=\"...\")\n- Search code: mcp__dope-context__search_code(query=\"...\")\n- List directories: mcp__serena-v2__list_dir(relative_path=\"...\")\n- Find symbols: mcp__serena-v2__find_symbol(query=\"...\")\n- Navigate: mcp__serena-v2__goto_definition(...)\n\nALLOWED BASH:\n- Git: git status, commit, push, diff, log\n- Docker: docker ps, logs, exec\n- System: python, pytest, npm, pip\n- File ops: mkdir, rm (not reading)\n\nWHY: MCP tools provide ADHD optimizations (max 10 results, progressive disclosure, complexity scoring), LSP intelligence, caching, and context generation that native tools lack.\n\nSELF-CHECK BEFORE OPERATIONS:\n1. Reading code file? \u2192 Use Serena MCP\n2. Searching code? \u2192 Use dope-context MCP\n3. Listing files? \u2192 Use Serena MCP\n4. Using framework? \u2192 Query PAL apilookup first\n5. Made decision? \u2192 Log to ConPort\n\nViolation detected in session 2025-10-23 - logged for prevention.",
./scripts/deploy/migration/conport_export.json:7173:      "description": "**VIOLATION INCIDENT**: Session 2025-10-24 - Multiple MCP-first rule violations during file cleanup\n\n**VIOLATIONS COMMITTED**:\n\n1. \u274c `ls -la .claude/personas/` \n   \u2705 CORRECT: `mcp__serena-v2__list_dir(relative_path=\".claude/personas\")`\n   \n2. \u274c `wc -l services/conport_kg/*.md`\n   \u2705 CORRECT: `mcp__serena-v2__read_file()` for each file to check size\n   \n3. \u26a0\ufe0f `rm` for untracked files - ACCEPTABLE but should explain\n   \u2705 BETTER: Explain \"These are untracked, safe to `rm`\" before deletion\n\n**WHY VIOLATIONS HAPPENED**:\n- Speed bias: Fell into bash habits for \"quick checks\"\n- File type confusion: Treated markdown summaries as \"not code\" (WRONG - MCP for ALL files)\n- Deletion shortcut: Used `rm` without explanation\n\n**CORRECT WORKFLOW**:\n```python\n# Check directory contents\nmcp__serena-v2__list_dir(relative_path=\"path/to/dir\")\n\n# Read file to check size/content\nmcp__serena-v2__read_file(relative_path=\"path/to/file.md\")\n\n# Search for patterns\nmcp__dope-context__search_code(query=\"pattern\")\n\n# Delete untracked files (OK to use rm, but explain)\nrm untracked_file.txt  # ACCEPTABLE for untracked files\n\n# Delete tracked files (ALWAYS use git)\ngit rm file.txt  # Tracked files\n```\n\n**SELF-CHECK BEFORE OPERATIONS**:\n1. About to list directory? \u2192 Use Serena list_dir\n2. About to check file size? \u2192 Use Serena read_file\n3. About to search files? \u2192 Use dope-context search\n4. About to delete tracked file? \u2192 Use git rm\n5. About to delete untracked? \u2192 rm OK, but EXPLAIN why\n\n**GIT-SAFE DELETION RULES**:\n- Untracked files: `rm` is safe (never in git)\n- Tracked files: `git rm` REQUIRED (preserves history)\n- When unsure: `git status` first to check if tracked\n\n**ADHD BENEFIT**: MCP tools provide progressive disclosure, complexity scoring, max 10 results - native bash doesn't.\n\n**ENFORCEMENT**: This pattern logged as reminder. Pattern #2 already documents core rules.",

./docs/04-explanation/serena-v2-technical-deep-dive.md:29:Serena v2 emerged from a critical architectural pivot documented in **Decision #84** (2025-09-29). Initial analysis revealed that Dopemux's existing `claude-context` service already provided sophisticated semantic code search with Milvus vector storage (OpenAI 3072-dim embeddings, HNSW indexing). Rather than duplicate this infrastructure, Serena v2 was redesigned as a **Navigation Intelligence Enhancement Layer** that integrates with existing search while adding LSP-based structural analysis, adaptive learning, and ADHD-optimized cognitive load management.

./reports/conport_sqlite_exports/20260206T143748Z/import_bundles/__Users__hue__code__dopemux-mvp__context_portal__context_db__conport_import_bundle.json:74:      "rationale": "Comprehensive Zen thinkdeep analysis validated all architecture synthesis claims about search/retrieval layer. ConPort uses 384-dim all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings (both core/embedding_service.py and v2/embedding_pipeline.py) vs dope-context's 1024-dim Voyage AI embeddings, confirming +35-67% quality gap. dope-context has best-in-class hybrid search architecture (dense multi-vector + BM25 sparse + Voyage rerank with ADHD progressive disclosure). ./reports/conport_sqlite_exports/20260206T143748Z/import_bundles/__Users__hue__code__dopemux-mvp__context_portal__context_db__conport_import_bundle.json:75:      "implementation_details": "Revised consolidation plan: Task 2.2 (1 day) - Remove ConPort semantic search: delete embedding_service.py and embedding_pipeline.py, keep PostgreSQL FTS for decisions, remove Qdrant integration plans. Task 2.3 (3 days) - Migrate dope-context from Qdrant to Milvus: export indexes, update vector_store.py, re-index code/docs, single vector DB for all services. Benefits: $0 embedding costs for ConPort (vs $0.12/1M tokens), simpler architecture, FTS proven adequate for decisions (<5ms queries), single vector DB (Milvus), prevents Qdrant in-memory data loss. Alternative Option A (synthesis plan): upgrade ConPort to Voyage 1024-dim for +35-67% quality but adds cost and complexity. Recommend Option B (simplified removal).",
./reports/conport_sqlite_exports/20260206T143748Z/import_bundles/__Users__hue__code__dopemux-mvp__context_portal__context_db__conport_import_bundle.json:92:      "rationale": "Architecture consolidation analysis revealed critical ADHD logic fragmentation across 4 services (Serena, ADHD Engine, ConPort, dope-context) with 23+ hardcoded thresholds causing inconsistency. Centralized ADHDConfigService with client library pattern provides single source of truth, user personalization, fault tolerance, and 75% maintenance reduction.",
./reports/conport_sqlite_exports/20260206T143748Z/import_bundles/__Users__hue__code__dopemux-mvp__context_portal__context_db__conport_import_bundle.json:93:      "implementation_details": "**Fragmentation Evidence:**\n- Serena v2: 10 hardcoded limits (max_results=10, complexity_threshold=0.7, focus_limit=5, context_depth=3)\n- ADHD Engine: 15 thresholds (monitoring intervals 60-300s, energy levels 0.2-0.9, cognitive load 0.2-0.8)\n- ConPort KG: 5 values (flow_threshold=900s, context_switches=5, cognitive_load_threshold=0.7)\n- dope-context: 2 limits (top_n_display=10, max_cache=40)\n\n**Inconsistencies Found:**\n- Cognitive load \"high\" varies: 0.6 (Serena) vs 0.7 (ConPort) vs 0.8 (ADHD Engine)\n- Progressive disclosure: 10 (general) vs 5 (focus mode) vs 40 (cached)\n\n**Solution: ADHDConfigService Architecture**\n1. Create dopemux-core/adhd module with unified ADHDThresholds schema (30+ fields)\n2. Build ADHDConfigClient with 5-minute caching (<1ms cache hits)\n3. Enhance ADHD Engine with GET /api/v1/config/thresholds endpoint\n4. Migrate services with feature flags for gradual rollout\n5. Fallback to safe defaults for fault tolerance\n\n**Implementation Phases (7 days):**\n- Week 1: Foundation (dopemux-core module, 2d) + API layer (ADHD Engine endpoint, 1d)\n- Week 2: Migration (Serena\u2192dope-context\u2192ConPort, 3d) + Validation (1d)\n\n**Benefits:**\n- Zero hardcoded thresholds (100% centralized)\n- Consistent values across all services\n- User-specific personalization enabled\n- 75% reduction in maintenance burden\n- Easy A/B testing (change once, affects all)\n\n**Risk Mitigations:**\n- Network latency: 5-min client caching\n- ADHD Engine failure: Fallback to safe defaults\n- Migration complexity: Feature flags for gradual rollout\n- Performance: Staggered cache expiry for even load\n\n**Files Analyzed:**\n- /Users/hue/code/dopemux-mvp/services/serena/v2/adhd_features.py\n- /Users/hue/code/dopemux-mvp/services/adhd_engine/engine.py\n- /Users/hue/code/dopemux-mvp/services/adhd_engine/config.py\n- /Users/hue/code/dopemux-mvp/services/conport_kg/adhd_query_adapter.py\n- /Users/hue/code/dopemux-mvp/services/dope-context/src/rerank/voyage_reranker.py\n\n**Enhanced vs Synthesis:**\nExtends original Task 2.3 (2 days) with client library pattern, fault tolerance, performance optimization, and realistic 7-day timeline. Adds user personalization capability not in synthesis.",
./reports/conport_sqlite_exports/20260206T143748Z/import_bundles/__Users__hue__code__dopemux-mvp__context_portal__context_db__conport_import_bundle.json:106:      "rationale": "Systematic Zen thinkdeep analysis revealed significant MCP infrastructure duplication and separation violations across 6 active MCP servers (context7, zen, conport, serena, gptr-mcp, claude-context). Found 5 infrastructure duplication categories: (1) API clients - 4 servers use OpenAI, 2 use VoyageAI with no coordination; (2) Embeddings - 2 separate pipelines (ConPort 384-dim vs dope-context 1024-dim); (3) Vector DBs - 3 approaches (Qdrant, Milvus, FTS); (4) Databases - ConPort split-brain across 2 PostgreSQL; (5) Coordination gap - Integration Bridge unused. Identified 3 separation violations: overlapping search (ConPort + dope-context), ADHD fragmentation (23+ thresholds across 4 servers), no shared utilities. 3-tier consolidation strategy maintains MCP independence while eliminating duplication through shared core library (dopemux-core), infrastructure consolidation (1 PostgreSQL, 1 Milvus, centralized embeddings), and clarified Integration Bridge routing (cross-plane only). Aligns with Decisions #4 (storage), #5 (search), #6 (ADHD).",
./reports/conport_sqlite_exports/20260206T143748Z/import_bundles/__Users__hue__code__dopemux-mvp__context_portal__context_db__conport_import_bundle.json:107:      "implementation_details": "**Evidence from docker-compose.unified.yml:**\n- 6 active MCP servers: context7 (3002), zen (3003), conport (3004), serena (3006), claude-context (3007), gptr-mcp (3009)\n- 2 disabled: task-master-ai (3005), leantime-bridge (3015)\n- Infrastructure: 2 PostgreSQL (5432, 5455), 2 Redis (6379, 6380), 1 MySQL (3306), 3 Milvus components, Integration Bridge (3016)\n\n**5 Infrastructure Duplication Categories:**\n1. **API Client Duplication**: OpenAI key in 4 servers (zen, conport, gptr-mcp, claude-context); VoyageAI in 2 (conport, claude-context) - no connection pooling or rate limit coordination\n2. **Embedding Service Duplication**: ConPort embedding_service.py (384-dim all-MiniLM) vs dope-context VoyageEmbedder (1024-dim) - 3x API cost, quality gap\n3. **Vector DB Redundancy**: Milvus (claude-context only), Qdrant (in-memory data loss), ConPort FTS fallback - migration incomplete\n4. **Database Split-Brain**: ConPort uses postgres-primary:5432 AND postgres-age:5455 - consistency risk per Decision #4\n5. **Coordination Gap**: Integration Bridge exists but MCP servers don't use it - direct service-to-service communication\n\n**3 Separation Violations:**\n1. **Overlapping Search**: ConPort + dope-context both do semantic search with different embeddings (Decision #5 resolves by removing ConPort search)\n2. **ADHD Fragmentation**: 23+ hardcoded thresholds across ADHD Engine (15), Serena (10), ConPort (5), dope-context (2) - Decision #6 resolves with ADHDConfigService\n3. **No Shared Infrastructure**: Each MCP isolated, duplicated code for API clients, caching, error handling\n\n**3-Tier Consolidation Strategy:**\n\n**Tier 1: Shared Core Library (dopemux-core)** - NEW\n- Unified API client manager (OpenAI, VoyageAI, Gemini) with connection pooling\n- Shared embedding service wrapper (delegates to dope-context)\n- ADHDConfigClient (connects to ADHDConfigService from Decision #6)\n- Common error handling, logging, health check patterns\n- Benefits: -60% code duplication, consistent API usage, centralized rate limiting\n- Timeline: 3 days\n\n**Tier 2: Infrastructure Consolidation** - CRITICAL\n- Database: Test PostgreSQL AGE+asyncpg compatibility (Task 1.1.1), merge or add sync layer (5d)\n- Vector DB: Complete Qdrant\u2192Milvus migration for dope-context (5d) - from Decision #4\n- Embeddings: Remove ConPort embedding_service.py, use dope-context only (1d) - from Decision #5\n- Timeline: 7 days (parallel tasks)\n\n**Tier 3: MCP Separation Strategy** - MAINTAIN INDEPENDENCE\n- Keep 6 MCP servers separate with distinct responsibilities:\n  * context7: External docs API (no infrastructure overlap)\n  * zen: Multi-model orchestration (stateless)\n  * conport: Decision authority (uses shared core for embeddings)\n  * serena: LSP server (filesystem cache, no DB)\n  * gptr-mcp: Research-specific (Tavily dependency)\n  * claude-context: Search authority (owns Milvus)\n- Rationale: Each has distinct responsibility per Two-Plane Architecture, no capability overlap after Decision #5\n- Timeline: 5 days for MCP updates to use dopemux-core\n\n**Integration Bridge Routing Rules** - CLARIFIED\n- **Cross-Plane Communication**: PM Plane \u2194 Cognitive Plane MUST route through Integration Bridge (port 3016)\n- **Cognitive Plane Internal**: Direct MCP-to-MCP allowed (same plane)\n- **Status Updates**: Only through Leantime Bridge \u2192 Integration Bridge \u2192 Leantime\n- **Decision Logging**: Direct to mcp-conport (cognitive plane authority)\n- Bridge responsibility: Event routing between planes, not general message bus\n\n**Implementation Roadmap (17 days):**\n- **Phase 1: Foundation** (Week 1, 5d): Create dopemux-core package (3d) + PostgreSQL AGE test (2d)\n- **Phase 2: Infrastructure** (Week 2, 7d): Qdrant\u2192Milvus (5d) + Remove ConPort embeddings (1d) + ADHD centralization (7d overlap)\n- **Phase 3: Integration** (Week 3, 5d): Update MCPs to use dopemux-core (3d) + Bridge routing rules (2d)\n\n**Expected Outcomes:**\n- Containers: 19 \u2192 16 (-16%)\n- Databases: 2 PostgreSQL \u2192 1 (or sync layer if AGE incompatible)\n- Vector DBs: 1 Milvus (remove Qdrant)\n- Code duplication: -60% through shared core\n- ADHD consistency: 100% via ADHDConfigService\n- Deployment complexity: -40%\n\n**Risk Mitigations:**\n- PostgreSQL AGE incompatibility \u2192 fallback sync layer\n- Migration complexity \u2192 feature flags for gradual rollout\n- Breaking changes \u2192 dopemux-core versioning with compatibility matrix\n\n**Files Analyzed:**\n- /Users/hue/code/dopemux-mvp/docker-compose.unified.yml\n- /Users/hue/code/dopemux-mvp/docs/ARCHITECTURE-CONSOLIDATION-SYNTHESIS.md\n- /Users/hue/code/dopemux-mvp/services/conport/src/context_portal_mcp/core/embedding_service.py\n- /Users/hue/code/dopemux-mvp/services/dope-context/src/search/hybrid_search.py\n\n**Validation:**\nAll findings cross-referenced with Decisions #4 (storage), #5 (search/retrieval), #6 (ADHD mechanisms) and architecture synthesis document. Strategy addresses root causes systematically with realistic timeline.",

Phantom Orchestrator** (CRITICAL):\n- Documentation: \"Integration Bridge for cross-plane event routing and orchestration\"\n- Reality: Read-only KG gateway with 5 GET endpoints only\n- Missing: Write endpoints (POST/PUT), event routing, orchestration logic\n- Impact: False architectural assumptions, no actual cross-plane integration\n\n**2. Phantom Orchestrator** (CRITICAL):\n- Documentation: \"Integration Bridge for cross-plane event routing and orchestration\"\n- Reality: Read-only KG gateway with 5 GET endpoints only\n- Missing: Write endpoints (POST/PUT), event routing, orchestration logic\n- Impact: False architectural assumptions, no actual cross-plane integration\n\n**2. direct service-to-service communication\n\n**3 Separation Violations:**\n1. **Overlapping Search**: ConPort + dope-context both do semantic search with different embeddings (Decision #5 resolves by removing ConPort search)\n2. **ADHD Fragmentation**: 23+ hardcoded thresholds across ADHD Engine (15), Serena (10), ConPort (5), dope-context (2) - Decision #6 resolves with ADHDConfigService\n3. **No Shared Infrastructure**: Each MCP isolated, duplicated code for API clients, caching, error handling\n\n**3-Tier Consolidation Strategy:**\n\n**Tier 1: Shared Core Library (dopemux-core)** - Phantom Orchestrator** (CRITICAL):\n- Documentation: \"Integration Bridge for cross-plane event routing and orchestration\"\n- Reality: Read-only KG gateway with 5 GET endpoints only\n- Missing: Write endpoints (POST/PUT), event routing, orchestration logic\n- Impact: False architectural assumptions, no actual cross-plane integration\n\n**2. Isolated Islands** (HIGH):\n- Zero MCP-to-MCP communication despite same Cognitive Plane\n- Each MCP completely isolated, no service coordination\n- Impact: No delegation, duplicated external API calls, no shared caching\n- Example: mcp-claude-context and mcp-conport both call VoyageAI independently\n\n**3. Synchronous API Gauntlet** (MEDIUM):\n- 4 MCPs independently call OpenAI (zen, conport, gptr-mcp, claude-context)\n- 2 MCPs independently call VoyageAI (conport, claude-context)\n- No connection pooling, no rate limit coordination\n- Impact: 3-4x API costs, potential rate limit violations, no deduplication\n\n**6. ConPort Split-Brain Communication** (CRITICAL - from Decision #4):\n- ConPort writes to TWO PostgreSQL: primary:5432 + age:5455\n- Integration Bridge queries postgres-age (third dependency)\n- Impact: Data consistency risk, transaction boundaries unclear\n\n**7. No Circuit Breakers** (LOW):\n- No fault isolation between services\n- If OpenAI fails, 4 MCP servers fail simultaneously\n- No graceful degradation or retry coordination\n\n**Communication Patterns Analysis:**\n\n**Actual Patterns** (Evidence-based):\n1. Client \u2192 MCP: stdio/SSE on ports 3002-3009 (working)\n2. MCP \u2192 Infrastructure: Direct DB/API calls (working but duplicated)\n3. PM \u2192 Cognitive (read): Leantime \u2192 Integration Bridge \u2192 ConPort KG (working, limited)\n4. x_source_plane, PM (read+events), Cognitive (full CRUD)\n- Timeline: 9 days (parallel with dopemux-core)\n\n**Optimization #2: MCP Service Mesh** (7 days, HIGH):\n- Service registry in Redis PM \u2192 Cognitive (read): Leantime \u2192 Integration Bridge \u2192 ConPort KG (working, limited)\n4. Cognitive Internal: NONE (expected but not implemented)\n\n**Missing Patterns** (Documented but absent):\n1. Cross-plane write operations\n2. Event routing (pub/sub)\n3. MCP orchestration/coordination\n4. x_source_plane, PM (read+events), Cognitive (full CRUD)\n- Timeline: 9 days (parallel with dopemux-core)\n\n**Optimization #2: MCP Service Mesh** (7 days, HIGH):\n- Service registry in Redis 7 days (Week 2)\n\n**Optimization #3: Shared API Client Pool** (3 days, HIGH - from Decision #7):\n- dopemux-core package with unified OpenAI/VoyageAI/Gemini clients\n- Connection pooling (max 10 concurrent), rate limit coordination\n- Benefits: -75% API calls through deduplication\n- Timeline: 3 days (Phase 1 of Decision #7)\n\n**Optimization #4: Fix Unknown Decision Flow** (4 days, CRITICAL):\n- Document current flow: Trace ConPort MCP database writes\n- Implement standard flow: Any service \u2192 mcp-conport.log_decision() \u2192 postgres-age\n- Tracing: Add request_id header for end-to-end tracking\n- Timeline: 4 days (Week 2)\n\n**Optimization #5: Activate Redis Event Bus** (4 days, MEDIUM):\n- Event channels: pm_plane_events, cognitive_plane_events, adhd_events, ./reports/conport_sqlite_exports/20260206T144006Z/quarantine__2026-02-04__SYSTEM_ARCHIVE__db_backups__context_20251024_181450_db/decisions.jsonl:70:{"id": 70, "timestamp": "2025-10-16T19:54:19+00:00", "summary": "Dope-Context Production Fixes: Added error handling, BM25 building, component caching, and incremental indexing", "rationale": "Implemented critical fixes to make dope-context production-ready and align with Anthropic's contextual retrieval research. Now matches Anthropic's full contextual retrieval pipeline: contextual embeddings (35%) + BM25 (14%) + reranking (18%) = 67% error reduction.", "implementation_details": "Modified files: (1) server.py: Added 5 LRU cache functions, comprehensive try/except blocks in _search_code_impl, BM25 building in _index_workspace_impl (line 195-220), BM25 loading in search (line 395-410), incremental reindex in _sync_workspace_impl (line 951-1014). (2) dense_search.py: Added get_all_payloads() method using Qdrant scroll API (line 443-489). Total changes: ~200 lines added. Performance impact: Component caching saves ~450ms per search (10x improvement), BM25 adds keyword matching (14% retrieval improvement per Anthropic), incremental indexing avoids full reindex (60x faster for small changes).", "tags": ["dope-context", "production-fixes", "bm25", "caching", "incremental", "anthropic-research", "contextual-retrieval"]}
./reports/conport_sqlite_exports/20260206T144006Z/quarantine__2026-02-04__SYSTEM_ARCHIVE__db_backups__context_20251024_181450_db/decisions.jsonl:71:{"id": 71, "timestamp": "2025-10-16T20:07:26+00:00", "summary": "Global MCP Configuration for Dopemux Platform-Wide Availability", "rationale": "Claude Code treats each git worktree as a separate project in ~/.claude.json. Without explicit configuration inheritance, each worktree started with empty mcpServers, even though they're part of the same repository. This caused \"No MCP servers configured\" errors in worktrees despite MCP servers running. Architectural decision: Dopemux is a development PLATFORM, not just a project. MCP servers and ADHD-optimized workflows should work identically everywhere (main repo, all worktrees, even unrelated projects if desired).", "implementation_details": "Migrated all 8 Dopemux MCP servers from per-project config to global config in ~/.claude.json. Before: Each of 11 projects had duplicate mcpServers config (88 entries total). After: Single global mcpServers section with 8 servers (context7, conport, exa, mas-sequential-thinking, dope-context, serena-v2, zen, gpt-researcher). Benefits: DRY principle (configure once), worktree-friendly (automatic inheritance), new projects get Dopemux superpowers immediately, consistent experience with global CLAUDE.md behavioral rules, maintainable (single source of truth).", "tags": ["mcp-configuration", "architecture-decision", "worktree-support", "adhd-optimization", "platform-design", "dry-principle", "decision-date-2025-10-16"]}
./reports/conport_sqlite_exports/20260206T144006Z/quarantine__2026-02-04__SYSTEM_ARCHIVE__db_backups__context_20251024_181450_db/decisions.jsonl:72:{"id": 72, "timestamp": "2025-10-16T20:08:00+00:00", "summary": "Dope-Context Performance Enhancement: Component Caching and Hybrid Search", "rationale": "Search operations had ~500ms overhead from repeatedly instantiating HTTP clients and Qdrant connections. Each search created new VoyageEmbedder, VoyageReranker, and MultiVectorSearch instances, wasting 350-550ms on connection setup. Additionally, dense-only search missed exact keyword matches that BM25 sparse search excels at. Solution: Component caching layer using @lru_cache to reuse instances (10x performance improvement: 500ms \u2192 50ms), plus BM25 hybrid search for best-of-both-worlds retrieval (semantic + keyword matching).", "implementation_details": "Added 5 cached component functions: _get_cached_embedder, _get_cached_reranker, _get_cached_vector_search (maxsize=20), _get_cached_contextualized_embedder, _get_cached_document_search. Caching uses API keys and collection names as cache keys. BM25 integration: Build index after vector indexing completes, persist to disk as pickle (bm25_index.pkl in snapshot dir), load on search with fallback to dense-only if missing. Enhanced error handling: API key validation, collection checks, graceful degradation on failures. Incremental sync: Optional auto-reindex with BM25 rebuild. Files: server.py (+300 lines), dense_search.py (get_all_payloads method). Performance validated: <200ms ADHD target met, cache hit ~50ms, first search ~150-180ms.", "tags": ["performance-optimization", "caching", "hybrid-search", "bm25", "adhd-target", "search-improvement", "error-handling", "code-review-approved"]}

./reports/conport_sqlite_exports/20260206T144006Z/quarantine__2026-02-04__SYSTEM_ARCHIVE__db_backups__context_20251024_181450_db/decisions.jsonl:137:{"id": 137, "timestamp": "2025-10-20T00:43:17+00:00", "summary": "Fix MCP token limit errors in dope-context with progressive truncation", "rationale": "MCP responses exceeding 10K tokens cause hard failures in Claude Code's transport layer. Dope-context search_code was returning full code snippets (5K+ chars each) \u00d7 10 results = 12K+ tokens, exceeding limit. Root cause: no token budget management in MCP response construction.\n\nSolution: Implemented 3-layer token budget system:\n1. Per-item truncation (2K chars/code snippet \u2248 500 tokens)\n2. Total budget tracking (9K target with 10% headroom)\n3. Progressive truncation (highest-scored results preserved, lower scores dropped if budget exceeded)\n\nValidation: All tests pass. Realistic 10-result search uses 39% of budget (3.5K/9K tokens), well under 10K MCP limit.", "implementation_details": "Files created:\n- services/dope-context/src/utils/token_budget.py (330 lines)\n  - estimate_tokens(): 1 token \u2248 4 chars (conservative)\n  - truncate_code_results(): Per-item + total budget enforcement\n  - truncate_docs_results(): Same for docs\n  - TruncationResult dataclass: Transparency about what was truncated\n\nFiles modified:\n- services/dope-context/src/mcp/server.py (4 changes)\n  - Added import: from ..utils.token_budget import truncate_code_results, truncate_docs_results\n  - Updated _search_code_impl(): Added budget_tokens parameter (default 9000)\n  - Updated _docs_search_impl(): Added budget_tokens parameter (default 9000)\n  - Modified search_all(): Split budget (4K code + 4K docs = 8K total)\n\nBudget allocation:\n- search_code standalone: 9K tokens (10% headroom)\n- docs_search standalone: 9K tokens\n- search_all combined: 4K + 4K + 1K overhead = 9K total\n\nADHD benefits:\n- Progressive disclosure preserved (highest-scored results intact)\n- Transparency (truncated field shows what was cut)\n- Consistent behavior (no random failures)\n\nTesting: test_token_limit_fix.py validates all scenarios pass with <10K tokens", "tags": ["mcp-integration", "token-limit", "dope-context", "adhd-optimization", "progressive-truncation"]}
./reports/conport_sqlite_exports/20260206T144006Z/quarantine__2026-02-04__SYSTEM_ARCHIVE__db_backups__context_20251024_181450_db/decisions.jsonl:138:{"id": 138, "timestamp": "2025-10-20T00:47:40+00:00", "summary": "System-wide MCP token limit security audit reveals 6 vulnerable servers (5 need fixes)", "rationale": "After fixing dope-context token limit issue (Decision #137), conducted comprehensive audit of all Dopemux MCP servers for similar vulnerabilities. Discovery: 10K token limit is a cross-cutting concern affecting ALL servers returning variable-sized content.\n\n**Audit Results**:\n- \ud83d\udd34 P0 Critical: Serena-v2 (read_file on large files), Desktop-Commander (base64 screenshots = 168K tokens!)\n- \ud83d\udfe1 P1 Medium: ConPort (bulk queries 100+ items), Zen (multi-step analysis accumulation)\n- \ud83d\udfe1 P2 Low: GPT-Researcher (research reports with many sources)\n- \u2705 Fixed: Dope-Context (3-layer progressive truncation)\n- \ud83d\udfe2 External: Context7 (not our code)\n\n**Critical Insights**:\n1. Base64 encoding kills budgets: 2MB screenshot \u2192 168K tokens (17\u00d7 over limit!)\n2. File reading without limits: package-lock.json (200KB) = 50K tokens\n3. Bulk queries need progressive truncation: 100 decisions \u00d7 150 tokens = 15K tokens\n4. Multi-step tools accumulate context: 10-step analysis = 20K tokens\n\n**Recommended Pattern**: Create shared `mcp_response_budget` utility for all servers to use.", "implementation_details": "**Audit Methodology**:\n1. Identified all active MCP servers in Dopemux\n2. Analyzed each tool for variable-sized response patterns\n3. Estimated worst-case token usage scenarios\n4. Prioritized by risk level and impact\n\n**Risk Assessment**:\n- HIGH (P0): Silent failures, broken core features, no workarounds\n- MEDIUM (P1): Failures on large datasets, degraded UX, partial workarounds\n- LOW (P2): Edge case failures, graceful degradation possible\n\n**Fix Priority**:\nPhase 1 (Week 1): P0 critical fixes\n- Serena-v2: Add max_lines=500, max_tokens=9000 to read_file\n- Desktop-Commander: Return file paths instead of base64 encoding\n\nPhase 2 (Week 2): P1 medium risk\n- ConPort: Progressive truncation for get_decisions, get_progress\n- Zen: Response field truncation for thinkdeep, planner, consensus\n\nPhase 3 (Week 3): Hardening\n- GPT-Researcher: Truncate source excerpts\n- Create shared mcp_response_budget.py utility\n- Document MCP token budgeting best practices\n\n**Shared Utility Design**:\n```python\n# services/shared/mcp_response_budget.py\n- estimate_tokens(text) \u2192 int\n- enforce_mcp_budget(response, budget=9000) \u2192 (truncated, was_truncated)\n- truncate_list_items(items, budget) \u2192 truncated_items\n- truncate_dict_fields(dict, fields, budget) \u2192 truncated_dict\n```\n\n**Documentation Created**:\n- MCP_TOKEN_LIMIT_AUDIT.md (comprehensive audit report)\n- Includes risk matrix, failure scenarios, fix patterns, lessons learned\n\n**Next Actions**:\n1. ./reports/conport_sqlite_exports/20260206T144006Z/quarantine__2026-02-04__SYSTEM_ARCHIVE__db_backups__context_20251024_181450_db/decisions.jsonl:143:{"id": 143, "timestamp": "2025-10-20T01:24:45+00:00", "summary": "Fixed critical workspace detection and multi-instance isolation bugs", "rationale": "User investigation revealed 4 critical bugs breaking ADHD context preservation:\n\n1. **CWD vs Git Root**: CLI used Path.cwd() instead of git root detection, breaking workspace detection from subdirectories and completely failing for worktrees.\n\n2. **Environment Not Passed**: MCP server startup subprocess didn't receive instance environment variables, making DOPEMUX_WORKSPACE_ID invisible to docker-compose. ALL instances used hardcoded default workspace.\n\n3. **Wrong Workspace in Env**: instance_manager.py set DOPEMUX_WORKSPACE_ID to main repo root instead of current worktree (actual_workspace). Instance B logged decisions to Instance A's workspace.\n\n4. **Fixed Ports**: docker-compose.yml used hardcoded ports (3004, 3006) preventing multi-instance from working at all - second instance failed with port conflicts.\n\n**Impact**: Context restoration broken, decisions logged to wrong projects, multi-instance completely non-functional. Core ADHD optimization promise (context preservation across interruptions) was broken.\n\n**Investigation Method**: Used dope-context search_code to find startup flow, grep to trace environment variable propagation, analyzed docker-compose for port configuration. Systematic code review revealed the issues were interconnected - fixing one without others wouldn't work.", "implementation_details": "**Files Changed**:\n\n1. **NEW: src/dopemux/workspace_utils.py** (174 lines)\n   - get_workspace_root(): Git root detection with worktree support\n   - Uses 'git rev-parse --show-toplevel' (returns worktree root for worktrees)\n   - Fallback chain: git root \u2192 project markers \u2192 cwd\n   - is_worktree(): Detects if workspace is a git worktree\n   - get_git_branch(): Returns current git branch\n\n2. **MODIFIED: src/dopemux/cli.py**\n   - Line 170: Changed project_path = Path.cwd() \u2192 get_workspace_root()\n   - Line 2565: Added instance_env parameter to _start_mcp_servers_with_progress()\n   - Lines 2585-2589: Create env_for_subprocess with instance vars merged\n   - Line 2617: Added env=env_for_subprocess to subprocess.Popen()\n   - Line 486: Pass instance_env=instance_env_vars to MCP startup function\n\n3. **MODIFIED: src/dopemux/instance_manager.py**\n   - Lines 261-263: Changed DOPEMUX_WORKSPACE_ID from self.workspace_root to actual_workspace\n   - Added DOPEMUX_MAIN_REPO for reference to main repo root\n   - Now properly isolates worktree instances\n\n4. **MODIFIED: docker/mcp-servers/docker-compose.yml**\n   - ConPort: Dynamic container naming, ports, workspace ID\n     - container_name: mcp-conport${DOPEMUX_INSTANCE_ID:+_}${DOPEMUX_INSTANCE_ID}\n     - ports: \"${CONPORT_PORT:-3004}:${CONPORT_PORT:-3004}\"\n     - environment: MCP_SERVER_PORT=${CONPORT_PORT:-3004}, WORKSPACE_ID=${DOPEMUX_WORKSPACE_ID}\n   - Serena: Same pattern (SERENA_PORT:-3006)\n\n**Environment Variable Flow**:\n```\ninstance_manager.get_instance_env_vars()\n  \u2192 instance_env_vars = {DOPEMUX_WORKSPACE_ID: actual_workspace, CONPORT_PORT: 3104, ...}\n  \u2192 os.environ.update(instance_env_vars)\n  \u2192 _start_mcp_servers_with_progress(project_path, instance_env=instance_env_vars)\n    \u2192 env_for_subprocess = os.environ.copy() + instance_env\n    \u2192 subprocess.Popen(..., env=env_for_subprocess)\n      \u2192 docker-compose reads ${DOPEMUX_WORKSPACE_ID}, ${CONPORT_PORT}\n      \u2192 Container gets correct workspace and ports\n```\n\n**Testing**:\n- Single instance: Backward compatible (defaults work)\n- Multi-instance: Port allocation (A=3000, B=3100, C=3200, D=3300, E=3400)\n- Subdirectory: Git root detection works from any depth\n- Worktrees: Isolated workspaces (Instance B doesn't see Instance A decisions)\n\n**Documentation**: Created WORKSPACE_MULTI_INSTANCE_FIX.md with complete analysis, before/after flow diagrams, and testing checklist.", "tags": ["critical-bug", "workspace-detection", "multi-instance", "adhd-optimization", "context-preservation", "worktree-support", "environment-variables", "port-isolation"]}

./reports/conport_sqlite_exports/20260206T144006Z/quarantine__2026-02-04__SYSTEM_ARCHIVE__db_backups__context_20251024_181450_db/decisions.jsonl:218:{"id": 218, "timestamp": "2025-10-24T01:58:23+00:00", "summary": "dope-context autonomous indexing design: Hybrid watchdog + periodic sync", "rationale": "Investigation revealed dope-context has excellent foundation (robust sync via SHA256 Merkle DAG, proven indexing pipeline, 98.9% test coverage, ADHD features) but requires manual user intervention for every sync cycle. Users must remember to call sync_workspace() \u2192 index_workspace() after code changes. This creates cognitive overhead and index staleness. Solution: Autonomous layer with three triggers: (1) Watchdog file system monitor for immediate response, (2) 5s debouncing to batch rapid saves, (3) Periodic 10-min fallback for reliability. Background async worker ensures non-blocking operation.", "implementation_details": "**Design - Four Components**:\n\n1. **WatchdogMonitor**: Uses watchdog library for file events\n   - Monitors workspace recursively\n   - Filters by include/exclude patterns  \n   - Debounces events (5s window for batching)\n   - Queues changes for worker\n\n2. **IndexingWorker**: Background asyncio task\n   - Processes change queue\n   - Calls FileSynchronizer.check_changes()\n   - Triggers incremental indexing\n   - Retry logic: 3 attempts, exponential backoff\n   - Error recovery\n\n3. **PeriodicSync**: Safety fallback\n   - Runs every 10 minutes\n   - Lightweight change check\n   - Catches watchdog misses\n   - Only indexes if changes detected\n\n4. **AutonomousController**: Coordinator\n   - Starts/stops all components\n   - Health monitoring\n   - Status reporting\n   - Graceful shutdown\n\n**New MCP Tools**:\n- start_autonomous_indexing(workspace_path)\n- stop_autonomous_indexing(workspace_path)\n- get_autonomous_status()\n\n**Configuration**:\n- autonomous_enabled = True (default)\n- debounce_seconds = 5.0\n- periodic_sync_interval = 600 (10 min)\n- max_retries = 3\n\n**ADHD Benefits**:\n- Zero mental overhead (never think about indexing)\n- Always up-to-date (auto-refreshes as you code)\n- Non-blocking (background operation)\n- Smart batching (5s debounce prevents excessive calls)\n\n**Files to Create**:\n- src/autonomous/watchdog_monitor.py\n- src/autonomous/indexing_worker.py\n- src/autonomous/periodic_sync.py\n- src/autonomous/autonomous_controller.py\n- src/autonomous/__init__.py\n\n**Integration**: Modify server.py to add 3 tools and optionally auto-start on MCP server initialization.\n\n**Cost**: Minimal (<$0.01/day for incremental updates on active project)", "tags": ["dope-context", "autonomous-indexing", "file-watcher", "adhd-optimization", "zero-touch"]}

System eliminates 100% of manual intervention - users never need to think about indexing again. Three-layer monitoring (watchdog + worker + periodic) ensures index stays current automatically. All 10/10 tests passing, 1,611 lines committed (755 production + 120 tests + 180 docs + infrastructure).", "implementation_details": "**Implementation Complete**:\n\nCode (755 lines):\n- src/autonomous/watchdog_monitor.py (224): File events, debouncing, pattern filtering\n- src/autonomous/indexing_worker.py (176): Background processing, retry logic, stats\n- src/autonomous/periodic_sync.py (130): 10-min fallback safety net\n- src/autonomous/autonomous_controller.py (225): Coordinator with global registry\n\nMCP Tools (+197 lines in server.py):\n- start_autonomous_indexing() - Enable auto-indexing\n- stop_autonomous_indexing() - Disable monitoring\n- get_autonomous_status() - Health and stats reporting\n\nTesting (120 lines):\n- test_autonomous.py: 10/10 tests passing\n- Component imports \u2705\n- Controller lifecycle \u2705\n- Status reporting \u2705\n- Registry management \u2705\n- Clean shutdown \u2705\n\nDocumentation (180 lines):\n- AUTONOMOUS_INDEXING.md: Complete usage guide, architecture, troubleshooting\n\n**Validation Results**:\n\u2705 All components import successfully\n\u2705 Watchdog monitoring starts/stops cleanly\n\u2705 Background worker processes queue correctly\n\u2705 Periodic sync schedules properly\n\u2705 Global registry tracks controllers\n\u2705 Status reporting comprehensive\n\u2705 Graceful shutdown works\n\n**Performance**:\n- CPU: ~0.1-0.5% (minimal overhead)\n- Memory: ~50MB\n- Latency: 7-15s from save to indexed\n- Cost: ~$0.01/day for active development\n\n**ADHD Win**: Developers never think about indexing again - it just works in background, always up-to-date, zero intervention.", "tags": ["dope-context", "autonomous-indexing", "implementation-complete", "zero-touch", "adhd-optimization"]}
